bull_bear.body: CFO of INR299cr in FY26 deployed to reduce working capital; no debt repayment planned beyond organic loan amortization; reinvestment prioritized into store expansion and inventory efficiency; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Competition intensifying in NCR (Croma, Reliance); price hikes in RAC and mobiles passed to customers, risking volume if demand elasticity kicks in; new geography entry (Calcutta) execution risk; dependency on monsoon and summer demand cycles
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and long-term oriented; CEO emphasizes control over customer experience, rejects franchise model for quality reasons; avoids giving FY27 guidance due to seasonal uncertainty; highlights operational rigor and margin discipline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite 140 new stores (<4 yrs), SSSG of 12.2% in Q4 implies strong underlying demand, not just store expansion; mobile ASPs rising despite industry-wide deflation due to premium SKU focus; NCR profitability achieved without franchise capital efficiency — a testament to operational excellence
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Growth is funded within a leverage band the deck presents as Net Debt to EBITDA and Gross Debt to EBITDA ratios reported for Mar-22 through Mar-26 alongside a Debt to Equity Ratio series; the deck's balance sheet shows Mar-26 non-current borrowings of Rs. 198.5 Crs and current borrowings of Rs. 692.6 Crs against Total Equity of Rs. 1,626.1 Crs.
- Working-capital release is the stated cash-flow priority — historical Cash Flow from Operations is shown as 116, 160, 176 and 452 across the FY22-FY26 chart, with Mar-26 Net Cash from Operating Activities of Rs. 443.7 Crs versus Rs. 175.8 Crs in Mar-25.
- Reinvestment is skewed to store rollout and owned property: Property, Plant & Equipment rose to Rs. 993.8 Crs (Mar-26) from Rs. 279.5 Crs (Mar-22), with Right of Use assets of Rs. 935.4 Crs reflecting the leased-store base.
- The deck states no dividend, buyback or explicit payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Large Appliances: 42% mix (down from 47%), driven by GST cuts and festive demand; Washing Machines & Panel TVs: double-digit growth; Refrigerators: stable despite price hikes; Mobile Phones: +28% growth, ASPs up due to premium model focus (avg INR35-40k); Accessories/Audio: higher-margin add-ons improving mix; Cooling: strong Q4 traction, inventory managed ahead of summer
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Describes itself as the "4th Largest Electronics Retailer in India" with "4 Decades" of experience, having begun with a single store in Hyderabad.
- Cluster-based model: "Deep penetration in the states of Andhra Pradesh & Telangana with a growing presence in NCR"; presence stated as 100+ cities and 6 states, with cluster detail of Telangana (112 MBO, 6 EBO, 42 cities), Andhra Pradesh (72 MBO, 52 cities), NCR (35 MBO, 1 EBO, 5 cities) and Kerala (1 MBO, 1 city).
- Multi-brand-outlet portfolio operated under own banners — Bajaj Electronics / Electronics Mart (208 stores), Kitchen Stories (5), Audio & Beyond (3), Easy Kitchen (3), The Charcoal Project (1) — alongside 7 EBOs.
- Claims brand-partnership strength: "We Partner with most of the world's best Brands and are a preferred distributor" and "Among organized retailers we drive the one of the highest ASP's for most OEMs"; deck lists Samsung, Sony, LG, Oppo, Vivo, OnePlus, Bosch, Whirlpool, Xiaomi, Blue Star, Lloyd, Faber awards/tie-ups.
- Differentiated in-store experience is stated as a lever: live product demonstrations, interactive trials, festival-themed event-driven selling and a consultative selling approach.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Divestment] The deck notes "16 Closures during the period were primarily driven by the divestment of IQ Apple Retail stores", and flags one store converted to an EBO.
- [Event platform] EMIL powered a "Smart Home Expo" described as "INDIA'S LARGEST SMART HOME EVENT", with tie-ups spanning Hisense, Bang & Olufsen, Funktion-One, Trinnov Audio, Buster + Punch and others across home cinema, audio and connected-home ecosystems.
- [Governance] Promoter-led board — Pavan Kumar Bajaj (Chairman & MD), Karan Bajaj (CEO & WTD), Astha Bajaj (Executive Director & WTD), with three independent directors.
- [Restatement] The deck cautions that "some of the line items of the financial statements for FY25 have been reclassified" and that FY25 indicators are recalculated in line with the reclassified statements.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin: 6.7% (Q4), 6.1% (FY26); mature stores: 7.3%, new stores: 3.1%; margin improvement driven by higher-margin accessories, reduced distributor reliance (only INR50cr/year), and improved SKU-level pricing discipline; GST reduction enabled volume-driven margin expansion
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: implied 7-10% FY27 (FY26 grew 7%); margin: target NCR EBITDA margin of 3-4% by FY28; order inflow: no explicit guidance; capex/commissioning: 12-15 new stores FY27, ~INR3-4cr/store avg, INR50cr+ real estate investment planned for Calcutta entry
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Entry into Eastern India (Calcutta) with 5-7 stores by Q2/Q3 FY27; potential future expansion into UP, Goa, Dehradun; no franchise model yet but under internal review
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q4FY26 revenue growth of 15% YoY and EBITDA margin expansion to 6.7% reflect successful execution of store maturity and category mix shifts, with mobile and large appliances driving demand; what matters is the sustained SSSG of 12.2% and NCR becoming EBITDA-positive, signaling scalable unit economics beyond core South markets.

meta.thesis: Strong Q4FY26 revenue growth of 15% YoY and EBITDA margin expansion to 6.7% reflect successful execution of store maturity and category mix shifts, with mobile and large appliances driving demand; what matters is the sustained SSSG of 12.2% and NCR becoming EBITDA-positive, signaling scalable unit economics beyond core South markets.
